name: codeshelf-light
description: Shows what your AI coding agents are doing (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor or your own) on CodeShelf Light RGB lights over WiFi or USB

codeshelfLight.enabled.description: Send agent status to the light

codeshelfLight.lights.markdownDescription: Your lights. Add them with **CodeShelf Light: Add Light** (it finds lights on your network and USB). Each light shows the most important state of the sessions it follows: all of them, or only some `agents` and `projects`.

name.description: Name shown in VS Code (renaming from VS Code also renames the light)

host.description: Address on your network, e.g. codeshelf-light-1a2b.local or an IP

enumDescriptions: WiFi, USB when WiFi does not answer

password.description: The light's page password, if you set one (needed to rename it from VS Code)

agents.description: Agent ids this light follows. Empty = all enabled agents

projects.description: Project folders this light follows: paths (~ and * allowed) or folder names. Empty = all

codeshelfLight.agents.markdownDescription: Agents that report their status. Presets: `claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, plus the `id` of any agent in `#codeshelfLight.customAgents#`. Hooks are added and removed automatically.

codeshelfLight.customAgents.markdownDescription: Your own agents. Each one maps the agent's hook events to light states (`working`, `attention`, `error`, `done`, `idle`, `end`). With `format` (`claude`, `cursor`, `copilot`) and `file` the hooks are installed for you; otherwise run **Copy Hook Command** and add it to the agent yourself. Example: `{ "id": "my-agent", "name": "My Agent", "events": { "start": "working", "ask": "attention", "finish": "done" } }`

stdout.description: event name (or "default") -> text the hook prints, if the agent requires output

file.description: Settings file to install hooks into, e.g. ~/.claude/settings.json

codeshelfLight.priority.markdownDescription: When several sessions are open, the state listed first wins. For example put `attention` before `error` to always see when an agent needs you.

codeshelfLight.codes.markdownDescription: Light state sent for each agent state: `T` working, `G` waiting, `Y` needs you, `R` error, `O` off. Colors and patterns are set on the light's settings page.

codeshelfLight.staleWorkingMinutes.description: A session stuck in 'working' with no hook events for this long (e.g. interrupted) is treated as done

codeshelfLight.doneToIdleMinutes.description: Minutes after which 'done' falls back to 'idle'. Both show 'waiting' by default, so this only matters with custom codes

codeshelfLight.remoteAnswers.markdownDescription: Claude Code: show permission requests and `AskUserQuestion` questions on the light's web page (WiFi) so you can answer from your phone. The terminal still asks if nobody answers in time. Only used for lights that have a page password set in `codeshelfLight.lights` (otherwise anyone on your network could answer).

codeshelfLight.remoteAnswerTimeout.description: Seconds to wait for an answer from the light before the agent asks in the terminal instead

codeshelfLight.chatHistory.markdownDescription: Claude Code: send your prompts and the agent's final answers to the Chat tab on the light's web page (WiFi), so you can read them on your phone. Kept in the light's memory only (last 8 messages, lost on restart). Only used for lights that have a page password set in `codeshelfLight.lights`.

codeshelfLight.remotePrompts.markdownDescription: Run prompts typed on the Chat tab of the light's web page (WiFi) with the `claude` CLI in a project folder, and show the answer there. **Anyone who knows the light's page password can make this computer run Claude Code**, so use a strong password. Needs a page password and VS Code open. Tools that need approval are denied unless `codeshelfLight.remoteAnswers` is on, then you approve them on the page.

enumDescriptions: Open a VS Code terminal with an interactive Claude Code, so you can watch it work. The answer comes to the page through the hooks, so it needs `codeshelfLight.chatHistory`. Approvals you do not answer on the page are asked in the terminal.

Open the graphical Claude Code window with the prompt filled in. You press Enter to send it (Claude Code cannot be told to send). Only for folders open in this VS Code window, others use the terminal.
Run `claude -p` out of sight and post its answer to the page. Nothing shows in VS Code.
codeshelfLight.promptMode.markdownDescription: How a prompt typed on the light's Chat tab runs.

codeshelfLight.chatProjects.markdownDescription: Extra project folders to offer on the Chat tab (`~` allowed). Open workspace folders and folders of recent agent sessions are offered anyway.

codeshelfLight.claudePath.markdownDescription: The `claude` command for prompts from the light. Empty finds the one that comes with the Claude Code extension, then `claude` on the PATH.

codeshelfLight.nodePath.description: Node binary used by the hook command

codeshelfLight.host.description: Address of the light on your network (name.local or IP). Rename the light with the 'Rename Light' command.
codeshelfLight.host.deprecationMessage: Moved to codeshelfLight.lights. Old values are migrated automatically.

codeshelfLight.connection.deprecationMessage: Moved to codeshelfLight.lights. Old values are migrated automatically.

codeshelfLight.serialPort.description: USB serial port of the light (e.g. /dev/ttyACM0, COM5) or 'auto' to detect an Espressif device
codeshelfLight.serialPort.deprecationMessage: Moved to codeshelfLight.lights. Old values are migrated automatically.
